## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to model per-tenant gating with latency awareness, using a sidecar to maintain state and a centralized store, plus end-to-end validation.

## Key Concepts
- Tenant-scoped health gate with per-tenant state
- Latency-aware 5xx degradation trigger
- Redis-backed counters and cooldown semantics
- Status exposure endpoints and lightweight validation

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal ConfigMap for thresholds
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-health-config
  namespace: cnf
data:
  latencyThresholdMs: "300"
  windowSeconds: "120"
  consecutiveFailures: "2"
```

```yaml
# Minimal test deployment with gateway and sidecar
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: cnf
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: cnf/gateway:latest
      - name: tenant-health-sidecar
        image: cnf/tenant-health-sidecar:latest
        env:
        - name: REDIS_HOST
          value: redis.cnf.svc.cluster.local
        - name: NAMESPACE
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: metadata.namespace
```

```yaml
# One-namespace manifest for validation
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: cnf
```

- How would you surface per-tenant health in a metrics dashboard and alerting rule?
- What testing strategy validates end-to-end degradation and reset behavior?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates advanced telemetry architecture, per-tenant observability, dynamic sampling strategies, and operational safety practices for CNF gateways at scale.

## Key Concepts
- OpenTelemetry, OTLP, trace context propagation, and baggage
- Namespace-scoped configuration and feature flags
- Adaptive sampling policies with latency-aware thresholds
- Canary rollouts and rollback safety

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf.trace
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  cnf.trace.enabled: "true"
  cnf.trace.sample-rate: "0.25"
  cnf.trace.target: "otel-collector.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local:4317"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0
      maxSurge: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: cnf-gateway
        image: cnf-gateway:latest
        env:
        - name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: cnf.trace
              key: cnf.trace.target
      - name: otel-collector
        image: otel/collector:latest
        args: ["--config=/etc/otel/config.yaml"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: otel-config
          mountPath: /etc/otel
      volumes:
      - name: otel-config
        configMap:
          name: otel-collector-config
```

## Adaptive Sampling Implementation
```go
func AdaptiveSampler(sampleRate float64, errorRate float64) float64 {
    baseRate := sampleRate
    if errorRate > 0.05 {
        return min(1.0, baseRate*2)
    }
    return baseRate
}
```

## Rollout Strategy
```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 5
      - pause: {duration: 5m}
      analysis:
        templates:
        - templateName: error-rate-check
        successfulRunHistoryLimit: 3
        failedRunHistoryLimit: 3
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement multi-tenant zero-trust mTLS using SPIFFE IDs, short-lived cert rotation, and KMS-backed CA in CNF gateways.

## Key Concepts
- SPIFFE/SPIRE trust domains per tenant
- CSR-based certificate rotation with short lifetimes
- Per-tenant mesh policies (Istio/OPA) for north-south and east-west traffic
- Workload identity verification via SPIFFE IDs

## Code Example
```yaml
# CSR bootstrap (outline)
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: gateway-td1-csr
spec:
  signerName: kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-clientSigner
  request: <base64-csr>
  usages:
  - digital signature
  - key encipherment
  - client auth
```

```yaml
# Per-tenant policy (outline)
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-td1-gateway
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        principals: ["spiffe://td1/ns/default/sa/gateway"]
    to:
    - operation:
        methods: ["GET","POST"]
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle cert revocation in case of a compromised gateway?
- How would you test cross-tenant isolation under peak load?

```yaml
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: featurepolicies.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              tenant:
                type: string
              allowedFlags:
                type: array
                items:
                  type: string
```
```rego
package gatekeeper.featurepolicy

violation[{"msg": msg}] {
  input.review.object.kind == "Deployment"
  annotations := input.review.object.metadata.annotations

  not featureR in policy.allowedFlags
  msg := sprintf("disallowed feature flag: %v for tenant: %v", [feature, input.review.object.metadata.namespace])
}
```
